quests.name: The Floor
quests.summary: Wake under Route 9, recover a routine, and earn a first supervised visit.

steps.objective: Stand up and check your coat.
Earn $50 through recycling, day labor, busking, or Sam's first flip.
Show Dana $50 in working cash and claim a shelter bed before curfew.
Keep the bed seven consecutive days and complete four work shifts.
steps.failure: A missed curfew resets only the bed streak, never story progress.

steps.objective: Attend supervised visitation at the Halvern Family Center.
Hear Dana's custody plan and unlock the streets and Army lines.

nodes.text: Dawn arrives as tire noise before it arrives as light. Your shoulder has taken the shape of a concrete seam. Something stiff presses against your ribs inside the coat.
Four dollars, a bus transfer dated yesterday, one clean sock. The stiff thing is still there.
The photo survived the rain. {{childName}} is laughing at somebody outside the frame. One shoe is untied. You remember taking it. You do not remember what happened after.
The crease crosses your own hand at the edge of the picture. Your hand had been steady then.
A shopping cart with two good wheels waits beside the pillar. The recycling center opens at six. Mara's Diner is already lit.
You look like the bridge charged rent.
Two dollars. The refill is me pretending not to notice.
Half a plate now, other half when you come back with pay. Don't make it a tradition.

choices.text: Keep it. Where is the recycling center?

nodes.text: Gus picks crews at the Industrial lot at seven. Show early. He respects clocks more than people.
Follow the river east until the smell changes from water to hot metal. Cart by the Route 9 pillar is nobody's until somebody pushes it.
Eat with both feet under you. Makes the day less likely to steal the chair.
You're blocking my light. Either come in or become architecture.

choices.text: Mara said you buy found things.

nodes.text: Mara says found when she means wet. I buy legal things with serial numbers still attached.
A receipt. A believable owner. Nothing with a child's name written on it. Standards get expensive only after you lose them.
Everybody needs work. I need the brass lamp from Nell's yard table on Carver. She wants five. The switch sticks. Make it not stick. Bring it here.
Brass lamp. Carver Street. Buy five, clean the switch, sell twelve. Seven dollars is small enough to teach you without lying.
Twelve if it works. Six if you tell me it works before I test it.
No. That was the whole lesson, delivered free.
Because she will charge me twenty and call it veterans helping veterans. You she might charge four out of pity. Let her keep the dignity and pay five.
Long enough to stop putting it first in a sentence. If you're thinking recruitment, think past the photograph at the desk.
The one where everybody came home. Now, lamp or doorway?
Check it twice. Trust the second look.
Name for the bed list. The legal one, even if you don't like it today.
No cash. Curfew at ten, chore at six, no using on the property. The fifty is not for us. I need to know one missed meal will not send you running at midnight.
Your intake mentions a child. Do you want their name used in the plan?
Then I write child and leave room. Room matters.
I can get you a supervised visit after seven nights in the same bed and four verified shifts. I cannot get you a second first impression. Be early.
The guardian agreed to ninety minutes. That is what I know. Don't spend the week inventing the rest.
C-14. Window rattles. Fold this intake copy into the latch.

nodes.stage: A family-center room. Two plastic chairs, a low table, a clock with a loud second hand. Dana sits by the door with a closed folder.
nodes.text: Hi.
I think that's what happens.
nodes.stage: They keep both straps of the backpack on.

nodes.text: I know that one. Grandma has it on her fridge, but not bent.
It looks like it.
nodes.stage: Almost a smile. The backpack comes off one shoulder.

nodes.text: Do I put my bag here or are we going somewhere?

choices.text: Here is good. We can draw.
We're staying in this room today.

nodes.text: Oh. Grandma said maybe the park.
Fine. We have fractions. I already knew halves.

choices.text: You used to split pancakes exactly down the middle.
Fractions get worse before they get better.

nodes.text: I don't remember that.
nodes.stage: They say it without cruelty. They pick a blue crayon.

nodes.text: What do you want me to draw?
Whose?
Okay.
nodes.stage: The crayon stops for one second. Dana looks at the closed folder, not at you.

nodes.text: That's not an idea.
The library has a window seat. Grandma lets me read past dinner if it's raining.
nodes.stage: The drawing is the window first, then the rain, then a small person inside. When the clock beeps, the blue crayon remains on your side of the table.

nodes.text: You can keep it. There are more in the box.
Dana knows the schedule.
nodes.stage: They look toward Dana, then back at you.

nodes.text: Bye.
nodes.stage: At the door, they lift one hand. Not a wave exactly. Enough to answer.

nodes.text: You showed up. That matters, so I am going to tell you what matters next without making it pretty.
Like a first visit. {{childName}} watched the door less by the end. Don't turn that into more than it is or less than it is.
Housing is thirty percent. Income twenty-five. Record twenty. Sobriety fifteen. Showing up ten. The judge sees a life as arithmetic because arithmetic fits in a file.
A shelter proves routine. An SRO proves a door. A two-bedroom gives the court somewhere to put a second toothbrush.
Not one big week. The court likes boring money. Four shifts, then four more. Pay stubs beat promises every time.

choices.text: I can keep working the street jobs.

nodes.text: Guaranteed pay, a possible voucher, and a real chance you are not here for the next hearing. Deployment complicates custody. Death ends the question. Recruitment will not put that on the poster.

choices.text: It may still be the cleanest road.
Then I stay here and build.

nodes.text: Then build slowly. Sam has work. Nia has faster work. Both roads leave receipts, even when nobody hands you one.
You can change paths. Life is not a class selection screen. The hearing is in thirty days either way.

events.effect: reset shelter streak and sleep outside
